subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: What should QuickStart do when Anthropic auth selects an Opus API-key model before the first terminal hatch?
rationale: Current source can support several fixes, but choosing a safer default versus warning/preflight versus documenting intentional Opus behavior changes first-run product policy and provider expectations.

options.title: Warn and offer recovery before hatch
options.body: Keep Anthropic available, but show a paid-credit/readiness warning before terminal hatch with in-product choices to change model/provider or continue intentionally.

options.title: Change the Anthropic first-run default
options.body: Use a lower-cost/default beta model for new QuickStart Anthropic setups while preserving existing configured model choices on upgrades.

options.title: Document current Opus behavior
options.body: Treat Opus as intentional and add docs/error guidance only, accepting that low-credit users may fail after first chat starts.

recommendation.title: Warn and offer recovery before hatch
recommendation.body: Keep Anthropic available, but show a paid-credit/readiness warning before terminal hatch with in-product choices to change model/provider or continue intentionally.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties the Anthropic default and current setup/error-copy paths to steipete's commits.
